solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The art class painted colourful headgear

indicators.note: a painted scene is a depiction made up afresh, so the letters before it are worked into a new picture

parts.note: all eleven letters of the phrase are the raw material

explanation.surface: Students in an art lesson daub paint over some bright hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid red colour and hats are things worn on the head, so the phrase is a description of bright headwear.

clue.text: Islamic judge in knitted jumper spoken of

indicators.note: something spoken of is said out loud, so we want a word that is pronounced like the clothing item

parts.note: a cardie is short for a cardigan, a knitted woollen top; in a non-rhotic British accent the R is silent

explanation.surface: A Muslim magistrate sits in court wearing a woolly sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; in southern British speech CARDIE and CADI sound the same because the R is not voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadi (also qadi) is a magistrate who rules according to sharia law in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Rather clever short story writer with no little following

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the following abbreviation must be taken out of the writer's title

parts.note: someone who writes fables, short moral stories
f. is the little abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A rather clever writer of short stories who lacks a modest fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little following' sounds like a small readership, but it is the one-letter abbreviation for 'following' used in footnotes (pp. 4 f.).
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, meaning more capable or somewhat cleverer than another.

clue.text: Extremely harmful ballgame in America? Nothing in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the zero is to be placed inside the phrase already built

explanation.surface: Is a ball sport in the USA dangerous, with no score at all?
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union is the ballgame; 'in it' tells you the zero goes inside what the first three words have built.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous describes something causing ruin or disaster, hence severely damaging.

clue.text: English run for property writ? No longer available

parts.note: leg it is slang for run away

explanation.surface: An Englishman flees from a property claim that is no longer on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer available' looks like a description of a property for sale, but it marks the writ as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegit was a historical legal order letting a creditor take over a debtor's land; it has since been abolished.

clue.text: Corporation starts to unpack loads involving barrows

parts.note: corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly

indicators.note: starts points at the opening letter of each of the next few words

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A company begins unloading cargo from wheelbarrows.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation here is old humorous slang for a large stomach. 'Involving' does double duty as the last word supplying a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrows are ancient burial mounds, and tumuli is the Latin plural for such mounds of earth over graves.

clue.text: Hard time in spring for office of Cossacks

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for time inside the word for spring

parts.note: to spring or issue from a source

explanation.surface: Doing hard time in the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring is the verb meaning to arise, not the season; T goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hetman was a Cossack military leader, and the suffix -ate makes the word for his position or territory.

clue.text: North Carolina inhabitant set on local cover

parts.note: an old verb (Shakespeare's tarre) meaning to urge or incite, as dogs to fight
a dialect verb (also hele) meaning to cover or hide

explanation.surface: Sounds like a resident fitted out with some neighbourhood insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are rare Chambers words: tar for egging on and heel as a regional word for covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar Heel is the long-standing nickname for a person from North Carolina, the Tar Heel State.

clue.text: Fools about in water channel

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the word for fools is read from the end

parts.note: tools are dupes, people used by others

explanation.surface: Idiots messing around in a ditch full of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloot (or sluit) is a South African word for a ditch or gully carrying water.

clue.text: Deputies failing on sharing facilities

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness

indicators.note: sharing suggests occupying the same space, so the short word sits within the facilities

parts.note: the gents is the men's lavatory

explanation.surface: Assistants who are bad at sharing the amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' is a euphemism for toilets; the gents is the British name for a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicegerent is someone who exercises power on behalf of a ruler, so vicegerents are deputies.

clue.text: Conceivably airline's ground transport for Indians

parts.note: flags that the wordplay is a whimsical imagined phrase rather than a fact

explanation.surface: Perhaps a carrier provides shuttle coaches for passengers from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conceivably' flags the whimsy: BA's bus, a British Airways coach, splits the word. 'Babu' is an Indian title and term for a clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Babu is a respectful Hindi form of address and also a term for an Indian clerk or official.

clue.text: Son at home is blocking deal? Sign of a bastard

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, here inside the trade word

parts.note: taken as written; it also serves the inclusion

explanation.surface: A boy staying in obstructs an agreement, a mark of illegitimacy.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the bar sinister is popularly a band across a shield said to denote illegitimate birth.

clue.text: Bones found in Indian set meal, not hot

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation that follows is dropped

parts.note: a thali is a platter of several small dishes served together

explanation.surface: Bones turn up in a mild Indian platter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tali is the plural of talus, the ankle bone that joins the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Appointed for a lawsuit, Democrat lawyer's first to probe two articles

indicators.note: to probe is to poke into, so these letters go inside the pair of articles

parts.note: an item is an article or thing; the second of the two

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the professional's title

explanation.surface: A Democratic attorney is first to investigate two newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles are A, the grammatical article, and ITEM, a thing; D and L go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad litem is Latin legal phrasing for someone, such as a guardian, appointed to act only in a particular case.

clue.text: Eccentric actor is a card

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or oddly arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An oddball performer is a real character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A card' looks like the slang for an amusing person, which fits an eccentric actor perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Taroc is a variant of tarot, naming both the old card game and the trump cards used for it.

clue.text: Faculties with debts, large uni finally liquidated

indicators.note: something liquidated is wiped out, so those letters vanish from the debts
finally selects the closing letter of the university word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: University departments buried in debt, with a big college finally wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculties' tempts as university departments, but it means talents; the L and I at the front of the debts are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Faculties in the sense of natural powers or capacities are talents, the same as one's skills or capabilities.

clue.text: Ye Olde Bull sticks with house wine ultimately

parts.note: gums is to stick, as with glue

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the drink word

explanation.surface: A pub called Ye Olde Bull stocks its own house wine.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an inn sign, but bull is American slang for a police officer or detective, and 'Ye Olde' marks the slang as dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumshoe is old American slang for a private eye or plain-clothes policeman, just like bull in that sense.

clue.text: Each book has pieces about parts of a tapeworm

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the combined string is read backwards

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as on price tags
short for liber, Latin for book

explanation.surface: Every volume contains extracts about a parasite's segments.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobila is the chain of segments that forms a tapeworm's body, so strobilae are its segmented sections.

clue.text: Know instinctively, time to stop a Greenlander

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the abbreviation goes into the Arctic native

explanation.surface: Sensing by gut feeling that it is time to halt a traveller from Greenland.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to understand by instinct or feeling without conscious reasoning.

clue.text: Experienced type, true pro theatrically

indicators.note: theatrically suggests a staged production, so these letters are put through a dramatic rearrangement

explanation.surface: A seasoned actor is a real professional on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouper, originally a touring actor, is a reliable veteran who carries on uncomplaining despite difficulty.

clue.text: Stick and where you should put it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to belong to or reside within something
second meaning: the two-word instruction pointing to a place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like an order to place something; the exclamation then answers where, as a cheeky pointing instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to be inherent, to exist permanently in or stay fixed as part of something.

clue.text: Keeper's rather stiff grabbing ball

indicators.note: grabbing means clutching, so the comparative holds the round letter inside it

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper is a bit rigid when clutching the football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' suggests a goalkeeper reaching for the ball; it is someone who stores things.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder keeps and accumulates possessions, often secretly, so is a keeper in that sense.

clue.text: Golfer on course repelled press with hooter

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the whole combination is turned around

parts.note: Ernie Els, the South African golfer
a run is a course or route

explanation.surface: A golfer on the links fends off journalists with a car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like reporters and 'hooter' like a horn; hooter is British slang for nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursle is an old variant of nuzzle, meaning to push or rub with the nose.

clue.text: Returns some poorest celeriac picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
some means a part, so the letters lie within the phrase

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Takes back part of the worst root vegetable harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' is the verb used of voters sending a candidate to parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters returning a member to parliament are choosing them by vote, which is to elect them.

clue.text: Screw cap of originality improved lager cans

indicators.note: cans as a verb means puts in a tin, so the rearranged drink encloses the single letter
improved means altered for the better, so the drink's letters are rearranged
the cap is the top, so take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A brewery boss improves a beer by putting it in cans.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British prison slang for a warder.
explanation.definitionFit: In prison slang a screw is a warder, the officer who keeps the inmates locked up.

clue.text: Fish ragu I'm cooking

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef announces they are preparing a meat sauce for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurami (gourami) is a freshwater fish of Southeast Asia, popular in aquariums and as food.

clue.text: Firm right away involved in expense

definitions.note: an old past participle of sting: overcharged

indicators.note: away means gone, so the abbreviation for right is taken out

explanation.surface: A company immediately gets dragged into costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like the business and the definition; it is the wordplay. This is an obsolete form of stung.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stung is to be charged heavily, so someone stung has been landed with a big bill.

clue.text: Left do captivated by casserole and squash

definitions.note: noun used as adjective: dilutable drinks are squashes

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside, so these letters go into the cooking vessel

parts.note: a diable is an unglazed earthenware cooking pot
ut is the old name for the note doh in sol-fa

explanation.surface: Leftover party food stuck in a stew, with a game of squash.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash is the British fruit cordial that is mixed with water before drinking, not the racket sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash is a concentrated fruit syrup sold to be thinned with water, which the drinks trade classes as a dilutable.

clue.text: Once fierce British army corps

parts.note: Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A British military unit that used to be ferocious.
explanation.definitionFit: Breme is an archaic word, found in Spenser, meaning fierce or harsh, hence the 'once'.

clue.text: Case of speech defect, say

indicators.note: a case is the outside covering, so take only the outer letters of the phrase

parts.note: the very first and very last letters of the two-word phrase

explanation.surface: An example of a speaking problem, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the outer letters of 'speech defect' plus a verb for say. 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stutter is a speech impediment in which sounds are repeated or blocked involuntarily, one instance of such a disorder.

clue.text: Dog and Duck: name seen up among foremost of Soho taverns

indicators.note: among places the pair between the selected letters
foremost picks the leading letter of each following word

parts.note: opening letters of the two words

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pair is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought

explanation.surface: The Dog and Duck, a pub name seen among the main bars of London's Soho.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dog and Duck is a real Soho pub, but here Dog is the definition. A duck is a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Snot, besides mucus, is slang for a contemptible person, just as dog can be an insult for a worthless one.

clue.text: No new option in play, they're stock themes

indicators.note: in play means being moved about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
No means without, so the abbreviation for new is dropped

explanation.surface: A dramatist has no fresh choice: plays keep using the same old ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Topoi, plural of topos, are conventional literary motifs or commonplaces of rhetoric.

clue.text: White-hot container used by dentist

parts.note: Dent. is a dictionary abbreviation for dentist and dentistry

explanation.surface: A tin bowl a dentist uses has been sterilised by heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Candent is a rare word for glowing with heat, from the same Latin root as candescent.

clue.text: Losing the first, begin again and drive into water

indicators.note: losing the first means the opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Having lost the opening round, a golfer starts over and hits into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Enew is a falconry term for a hawk driving its prey into water.

clue.text: Remarkable money brought back in notes

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the combined letters run the opposite way

parts.note: some as in 'that was some party'
M is an abbreviation for money supply in economics

explanation.surface: An exceptional sum of cash is returned in banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like banknotes, matching the money, but it means brief written messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Memos are short written messages, memoranda, circulated within an office.

clue.text: Adult censored must agree stories showing coarseness

indicators.note: must is a variant of musth, the frenzied state of a male elephant, so the letters run wild
censored means cut out, so the certificate letter is removed

parts.note: the twelve letters of the two words
A was the old British film certificate for adult audiences

explanation.surface: Censors must agree that adult tales are crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must' looks like an auxiliary verb but is the anagram signal, from musth, an elephant's frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossièreté is a French borrowing for rudeness or vulgarity, the quality of being gross or coarse.
